Uniform Title: *Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālinīkalpa* Manuscript: NGMCP manuscript 52, Reel no. B 116/13 Notes: Data entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the direction of Mark S. G. Dyczkowski.
Revision 0: April 28, 2017 Place of Publication: India Ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālinīkalpa
Oṃ, homage to Gaṇeśa.
In the *Śrīsāradātilaka*, within the dialogue between Rudra and Pārvatī at the root of Ugrarudrī, the ritual manual (*kalpa*) for the twenty-syllable Ucchiṣṭacaṇḍālinī will now be described.
Now, therefore, O Goddess, O beloved Mātaṅgī, I shall fully declare this most secret [mantra], which grants all desires, beginning with the word "ucchiṣṭa. 1.
The pacifier of all evils, the purifier of all; by which one may know the Divine.
They perform that rite and attain the state of peace. || 2 ||
The sky is the abode of the three vajras; it bestows divine nectar and destroys poison.
O Goddess, one who is possessed by hostility toward Brahmins shall be overcome by defeat. || 3 ||
O Supreme Goddess, together with the Vidyā, she is the destroyer of all sins;
O Goddess, when joined with the syllable Om, she bestows the fruit of heavenly bliss and royal happiness. (4)
"O Queen, this poison-encircled [ring] was accomplished by me after having heard [your request]."
Ignorance, when uttered even once, is the destroyer of rice and the slayer of Brahmins.
I bow to you, the Goddess who removes sins and bestows worldly prosperity upon the world.
If, however, she is desired by you, O Kārttikeya, when shall the Goddess ever appear?
1a) O Goddess, may you never at any time forget the happiness of the sacrifice performed on this day. || 6 ||
Then, when Ātmeśvarī had been made to lose her husband,
she became difficult to traverse like a mountain path, and she struck those who were distressed by suffering with terror.
A barren woman obtains offspring, a sick person lives a long life,
the indigent attains wealth, and one shall obtain knowledge and joy.
O Goddess, I shall proclaim the delightful *vidyā*-crop,
by which you may request [your desires], O Goddess, even without the exertion of a lowly loan.
First, one should offer an oblation (bali) together with the supreme mantra;
then, having meditated upon the recitation of the mantra, one should accomplish the goal through the fire-ritual (vaṃhya). || 10 ||
1b) O Great Goddess, I shall now tell you the mantra for recitation, which is glorious and full of flesh: first is the word *ucchiṣṭa*, and likewise *cāṇḍālinī* and *liccha*. 11.
Then, O Goddess, one should meditate upon Sumukhī; immediately after that, one should remember Mahāpiśācinī, who is dissolved therein. Then, beyond that, [one should remember] Layāvita.
O Great Goddess, the three syllables beginning with *ṭha*, joined with the *nāda* and *bindu* and accompanied by the *visarga*, bestow all spiritual accomplishments (*siddhi*).
Neither the nine years nor the nine months, nor the nine fortnights, nor the lunar days, nor the stars, nor the rule of the nine planets [is required]. (14)
There is no counting, no ninefold sacrifice, no serpent-consecration, and no ritual manual;
for those enemies of desire, anger is the primary cause of their destruction. 15.
O Fire of Existence,
for one who remains within this mantra, there are no difficulties whatsoever, nor is there thirst, nor the sound of obstacles.
O Goddess, Sovereign of the World, I shall describe his meditation according to his vow; O Goddess, at the time of eating, one should remember this most excellent meditation. (17)
2a) One should meditate on her seated upon a conch shell, clothed in red garments,
adorned with red ornaments, and resplendent with a necklace of gunja berries.
She has forty-six teeth, full and firm breasts, holds a skull-cup in one hand, and carries a rosary and a water-strainer in her other hands. (19)
[He saw] the lion-throne of Mābhinā, the Trikūṭa mountain, and the supreme sky;
[he saw her] with two arms and four arms, with three eyes and beautiful eyes.
Holding a noose, a *kuśa*-arrow, a bow, a palm-leaf fan, a lamp, and ornaments, she is adorned with red decorations and anointed with red sandalwood paste. || 21 ||

O Dear One, with a focused mind, one should meditate on the supreme maṇḍala of mantras by means of the left and right movements; then, one should offer the remaining portion as a bali-oblation while reciting the mantra.
2b) O Goddess, that [period] of foods occurs even without the performance of rites; I shall now describe the Dvāpara age, which yields fruit—listen, O Goddess. (23)
Having performed the offering of the recitation, one should afterwards undertake the ritual action;
having prepared the Caṇḍila-maṇḍala, the practitioner, being well-composed, should attend to the patient.
Having drawn a *jātrā* (cross) in the middle of that and likewise three, eight, and sixteen [squares], the practitioner should worship the goddess of the mandala with the root mantra. || 25 ||
Then the Goddess, having meditated upon it, remained established in the form of fire.
And for one desiring knowledge, [one should offer] honey, curd, white mustard seeds, and rice grains.
With sesame seeds mixed with *siddhārtha*, along with honey and the three Vedas (*traividyam*).
The oblation should be equal to a lotus petal, or provided with bilva leaves. || 27 ||
By means of the single thousandfold ritual, the king attains the state of being beloved.
3a) O Goddess, one should perform the homa with the flesh of a freshly slaughtered animal and net-meat. || 28 ||
One who has properly accepted the weapon attains fruitful knowledge;
and one should prepare [the offering] with the flesh of a goat together with honey. (29)
By performing the rite according to the procedure of a thousand [repetitions], the desired accomplishment will certainly be attained.
One who desires knowledge should perform the fire-oblation with the prescribed offerings while properly honoring the sages.
O Goddess, one who bows down should immediately recite the fourteen-fold Vidyā while wearing a garment stained with menstrual blood and drinking honey mixed with *abhaya* powder. (31)
The Great Goddess should perform the fire-oblation; by this she brings the three worlds under her control.
[She should do so] with the leaves of the *nāgavallī* in a fire-oblation accompanied by honey, clarified butter, and milk-rice (*pāyasa*).
By performing ten thousand repetitions of this single method, the accomplishments of wealth are attained.
By offering an oblation with the honeyed mouth of a rabbit’s jaw,
one obtains whatever one desires, even celestial women.
One who knows the mantras should kindle the funeral pyre, constructed with wood from the *dhatura* tree, using clarified butter.
One should perform the oblation with the Kaukilākāka mantra using the two lips, which brings about destruction. || 34 ||

3b) One should perform the fire sacrifice (homa) for the uprooting of enemies continuously on a Tuesday, according to the procedure previously described, while offering fuel from a funeral pyre into the fire.
One who knows the mantras should perform a homa with the feathers of an owl, a crow, and a vulture;
then, during the night, [the enemies] shall be filled with mutual strife and hatred.
By means of a homa sacrifice with owl feathers, a woman whose fetus has perished shall indeed obtain a child.
By consuming bilva leaves and clarified butter continuously for one month, even a barren woman shall obtain an excellent son who lives for a long time. (39)
One who desires good fortune and happiness should offer a *vaṃdhūka* flower together with grapes and honey to one who has become unfortunate or fallen from her station. (40)
By means of this yoga practiced for four months, the extraction of women will certainly occur:
daughters of gods, daughters of nāgas, daughters of yakṣas, and daughters of kiṃnarīs. 41.
The mother of Praveśavatī forcibly embraced him.
Having addressed Rekhādevī, he departed accompanied by Naja and Ācala.
O Goddess of goddesses, Great Goddess, bestower of the fruits of the left-hand practice (vāmācāra)!
By means of the yoga of the right-hand practice (dakṣiṇacāra), she becomes the granter of fruits. 43.
O Queen, by offering an oblation (bali) during the mealtime on that day, one crosses over the ocean of existence;
and by means of the mantra, one crosses over the eighth ocean of human rebirth while still impure from food.
Whether in a cemetery, in a deserted house, at a crossroads, in a place of old age, in the midst of the head, or even alone with Rāma; 45.
By offering an oblation, the Goddess will certainly become manifest before one's eyes;
when one desires the form of Bhairava in the city of Vīramayā. || 46 ||
The goddess described by Putana is the destroyer of all sins;
by the mere utterance of her mantra, she bestows all spiritual perfections.
Oṃ puṃ hrīṃ krīṃ ucchiṣṭacāṇḍāli nī sanmukhīdevi mahāpicāsinī hrīṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ svāhā— this is the mantra.
Now begins the section on the mechanical door.
4b) I shall now proclaim the great yantra-mantra, which bestows results when faced directly.
The three peaks, the eightfold, the sixteenfold, the eightfold, and four times four.

In the rites of immobilization (staṃbhaṇa), expulsion (uccāṭana), inciting enmity (vidveṣa), subjugation (vaśīkaraṇa), delusion (mohana), in battle, against kings, and in the perils of messengers; || 2 ||
O Goddess, this yantra, which is difficult even for the three worlds to obtain, is drawn upon the ground;
one should worship this yantra for all ritual purposes.
For the purpose of fame, one should write on a leaf; for the sake of a maiden, on a reed-leaf;
for killing, on an iron leaf; and for subjugation, in a vessel of bell-metal.
In the case of a dispute over a gift, in a legal proceeding, or in battle, one should employ that [mantra] for the sake of victory;
in battle, it shall cause the enemy's weapons to fail and reveal their magical illusions.
This supreme vidyā should be kept strictly secret and must not be given to just anyone;
it should be given to one of noble lineage, who is wise and has conquered his senses.
5a) O Goddess, one should accomplish the Great Vidyā in a grove; it brings about all accomplishments for men. After eating, O Goddess, one should recite the mantra daily. 7.
One should not perform recitation while impure; one should cause the mark to be applied while impure.
O Goddess, this is declared as the ever-granting [mantra] that bestows all accomplishments: *nisī nisī*. 8.
Those who delight in sensual desires, those who have accumulated stores of asceticism, those who wander about like poison, and those who abandon their cities;
those known as Śrīṣaṇḍas, those who are like fire, and those who are like elephants among men—they all serve the Liṅga.
That wonderful sacrifice of service—what else could it be but a thunderbolt adorned with flowers?
Thus is the ritual for the remnants; having prepared a mandala on a sacrificial mound, one who is composed should recite the four thousand [verses].
O Goddess, the knower of mantras should worship the mandala with the root mantra.
"Oṃ āgaccha trayaṃ hi jvālāye āsanaṃ namaḥ.
Thus is the invocation (āvāhana). Now, the fire-oblation (homa): with curd, white mustard seeds, and rice, one thousand [times] according to the prescribed rite.
4b) Chāṃ chīṃ chaṃ chaiṃ chauṃ chaḥ—by these, the King becomes subject to one's will; with the flesh of a cat, one should perform the oblation for the Goddess with speed.
Having mastered both weapons and non-weapons, he attains the supreme, divine accomplishment of weapons and non-weapons.
Maṃ māṃ mīṃ muṃ maiṃ mauṃ; salutations to the one whose eyes are like those of a cat. || 1000 ||
And by performing the fire sacrifice (homa) with goat meat, ghee, and honey, according to the procedure of one thousand repetitions, the accomplishments of wealth (dhanasiddhi) are attained.
Wealth: 1000. Acquisition: 1000.
chaṃ chāṃ chīṃ chraṃ chaiṃ chauṃ chaḥ ||
Homage to Bhujāmarddhanī.
For one who practices for the sake of knowledge or desire, one should perform a fire-oblation with sugar and honey.
O Goddess, let it be that he may instantly attain the fourteenfold knowledge.
puṃ vāṃ vīṃ kakuṃ caiṃ vauṃ caḥ.
Salutation to Vāyuvagāyī.
6a) [One should offer] into the cloth of a menstruating woman with honey and milk-rice.
Having performed the fire sacrifice (homa), this goddess will bring the three worlds under one's control.
Aiṃ rāṃ rīṃ ruṃ raṃ rauṃ raḥ.
Obeisance to Rāsavatī Mātaṅgī.
One should perform a fire sacrifice with honey on a Nāgavalī leaf for one who has committed a thousand offenses.
By means of ten thousand repetitions according to the prescribed rite, the desired accomplishment will certainly be attained.
The eight great siddhis: Aiṃ, Nāṃ, Nīṃ, Nuṃ, Naiṃ, Nauṃ, Naḥ; together with the honey extracted from the net of the Sadyāmā.
If it is joined with Cāṇḍālaka, the dragging down of one's existence will certainly occur.
Aiṃ cāṃ cīṃ cuṃ caiṃ cauṃ caḥ, O devourer of the māṃjārī, O Cāṇḍālī,
svāhā!
Together with meat mixed with honey and sugar, [the mantra] of the illustrious Vāsudeva is: aiṃ sāṃ sīṃ suṃ saiṃ sauṃ saḥ.

Salutation to Śiva and Satkī. By means of the application of the arm and the wooden staff, one performs the fire-sacrifice (*citāvahana*) and the self-homa (*svahoma*), which destroys enemies and subdues foes. *Aiṃ kāṃ kīṃ kuṃ kauṃ kaḥ*, salutation to the one who shatters the skull (*kapālabharchani*).
Urcāṭaṇa.
Upon the funeral pyre made of wood according to the previously described procedure, [he should offer oblations].
Having performed the oblation with an owl and a crow's feathers, one becomes submissive.
Urcāṭanā Aiṃ, obeisance to this Mālinī.
By means of the homa with the liver of an owl, one causes the miscarriage of a woman's fetus.
Having performed the fire-oblation according to the procedure for one thousand repetitions with a concentrated mind,
Aiṃ paṃ pāṃ puṃ paiṃ pauṃ paḥ.
Homage to the one seated upon a lotus throne.
One should consume bilva leaves and seeds continuously for one month without interruption.
O Manu, one who knows the three Vedas shall obtain a long-lived son.
Homage to Cala, Cīca, Cīcu, Cṛcīi, and Kalaradaputradāya.
Having plucked a *vaṃdhūka* flower and combined it with fresh honey, [one should offer it].
O Goddess, he shall become a bestower of good fortune and happiness even upon the unfortunate.
Aiṃ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ draiṃ drauṃ draḥ; obeisance to the one who possesses fortune for the unfortunate woman.
By means of this yoga, the summoning of wealth will certainly occur within six months.
A celestial maiden and a daughter of the Gandharvas and Nagas, afflicted by desire, came to a certain donor,
their eyes restless and their speech faltering.
One should not offer an oblation while impure; by such conduct night after night, the practitioner [is ruined].
Thus ends the Śrīpārvatīyodhasanmukhīkalpa, composed by the great god Ucāra within the venerable Viśvasāra.
Oṃ uciṣṭacāḍālinī, homage to the two thumbs (āṃguṣṭha).
O Goddess Sanmukhī, salutations with the two hands in the threatening gesture (tarjanī).
Svāhā to the powers; homage to the palms and backs of the hands.
To the outcaste woman of leavings, homage to the heart!
To Sumukhī on the head, svāhā!
Vauṣaṭ to the great Piśācinī Siddhiṣāyā!
Hrīṃ, for the armor, huṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ, for the three eyes, phaṭ svāhā; for the weapon, phaṭ.
This is the meditation that surpasses all other meditations.
